name: Ulam
overview: Ulam was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Eshek. His mention in Scripture is concise and focused on his lineage without additional narrative detail or personal attributes.
namesAndTitles: The name Ulam is a proper name meaning 'first' or 'leader.' This name is not indicated as being given by God but reflects a Hebrew term that may suggest a position of prominence or priority.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ulam as the son of Eshek, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family connections or relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ulam's significance in the biblical record lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Benjamin. His mention in 1 Chronicles 8:39 helps preserve the lineage and tribal identity important to Israel's history and God's covenant people. Though brief, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of the biblical record in tracing God's chosen people through generations.
